recent_posts.title: Landlord: a tenancy controller and experiment in AI driven product building
recent_posts.summary: Landlord is an experimental tenancy controller that automates compute-per-tenant provisioning using pluggable workflow providers like Restate. Built with Go, it manages tenant lifecycle through durable workflows, supporting Docker containers with plans for ECS, Kubernetes, and EC2. The project demonstrates spec-driven development with AI coding assistants, where detailed specifications enabled rapid development of a complex system that handles tenant creation, updates, and state management through a control plane API.

recent_posts.title: The enshittification of enshittification
recent_posts.summary: The term 'enshittification' has become overused to the point where any change to a product is viewed with suspicion. Not all venture-backed companies inevitably degrade their products - incentive structures matter. For B2B tools like Tailscale, maintaining a strong free personal tier isn't charity but essential business strategy: happy individual users become advocates who bring the product into their workplaces. The real revenue comes from companies, not individuals, so degrading the personal experience would destroy the primary customer acquisition channel. Trust compounds slowly and breaks quickly, and treating enshittification as inevitable removes accountability from companies that actually make poor choices.

recent_posts.title: An easy, realistic model for MCP connectivity
recent_posts.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has evolved rapidly from local stdio connections to remote HTTP servers, creating significant security vulnerabilities. The author demonstrates how Tailscale can provide a secure connectivity model for MCP servers by keeping them off the public internet while enabling remote access through private networks. The solution includes application-aware permissions using Tailscale's grants mechanism, allowing fine-grained control over which users can access specific MCP tools and resources. While this approach requires Go for server implementation and local client proxies, it offers a more secure alternative to exposing MCP servers publicly.

recent_posts.title: The Evolving Role of Developer Relations in a Changing Tech Landscape
recent_posts.summary: Developer Relations (DevRel) faces challenges as startups prioritize roles with clear, measurable contributions to revenue. The rise of Product-Led Growth (PLG) models and tightening VC funding necessitate a shift in how DevRel professionals align their activities with sales, marketing, and customer success. The future of DevRel involves embracing measurable outcomes and adapting roles to ensure long-term sustainability and relevance in the tech industry.

recent_posts.title: Free Kubernetes Load Balancers with Tailscale
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to expose Kubernetes workloads to the world without a load balancer using Tailscale. Tailscale allows you to access Kubernetes workloads using native Service and Ingress objects without paying for cloud provider load balancers.

recent_posts.title: Structuring your Infrastructure as Code
recent_posts.summary: The article provides guidance on structuring infrastructure as code for scalability and longevity. It discusses the concept of layers and suggests managing certain layers with IaC while manually handling others. It also explores the decision-making process for determining the placement of resources in the infrastructure. Additionally, it touches on the debate between mono-repo and multi-repo approaches for IaC and offers recommendations based on different layers. The article emphasizes the importance of encapsulating resource patterns into separate repositories and sharing them across projects.

recent_posts.title: IaC Ergonomics: Choosing an Infrastructure as Code Tool
recent_posts.summary: The article discusses the authoring experiences, execution experiences, and cloud provider experiences in Infrastructure as Code tools. It compares different tools like Terraform, CloudFormation, Crossplane, ARM, and Pulumi. It highlights the importance of considering programming language-based authoring experiences and provides a decision tree to help readers choose the right tool.

recent_posts.summary: Lee Briggs: Why does nobody seem to know what imperative and declarative actually mean? He says his job description does not expect him to continuously argue with people on the internet about what words mean.
